rows.what the ink shows: A tall opening stroke, an i-dot and a final upright survive, but two heavy horizontal cancellation strokes merge the medial bodies; the extra letters in Soient cannot be separated reliably from Soit.

The word begins with a long descending f and small loop, followed by a dotted medial stroke and tall l-like shoulder; its compressed trailing run matches the second visible facilement lower on this page.
A tall looped opening descends into joined low rounded strokes, followed by a separate hooked final s; the low ending resembles the page’s later alors.
After the distinct baseline Y and A there is one U, with a looped left arm, rounded bottom and upright right arm, rather than a pointed V. One separate multiprong star sits above its right side.
A short thick body and a detached upper dab remain, compatible with a dotted i, but the cancellation fills the s/i junction and prevents separation of the proposed letters.
The canceled superscript retains an apex and two separated descending feet, with the same A outline as the larger replacement below the delta; the center is heavily blackened.
A low open C curve meets a tall hooked f stem with a rightward cross-stroke; a separate short dot is visible above and to the right.

The crossed phrase has the tall initial loop and low n of On, a separate rounded a, then an ascending d followed by a low run with the final n/c humps; the cancellation covers parts of the word bodies.
A low initial co/m run rises into a pronounced p descender, followed by an upright l and the long crossed t ending. The descender distinguishes complète from maximale; the small accent is faint.
Between E and t are two compact thick horizontal bars; the upper stroke has no visible left-pointing angle of ≤.
The word begins with an s/p junction and a descending p, continues through a long low run with a crossed t, and ends in a small a followed by an upright l before the parenthesis.

The lower index has a closed low bowl joined to a distinct right descending leg, making it a-like rather than the nearby open E. Its upper attachment is crossed over, so lowercase a versus capital A remains unsettled.

An additional heavily struck fragment precedes the clearer Δ: its triangle-like head and lower E-A-E are partly merged with extra cancellation, especially around A. The later term distinctly has raised E, three lower letters E-A-E, and one A in parentheses.
